power.title: Power Analysis Check
report: No power analyses were detected.

::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

prereg_check.title: Preregistration Check

table.title: Do AI-assisted systematic reviews preserve methodological quality? A meta-research study of published systematic reviews in the large language model era
table.study_type: Observational Study - Data is collected from study subjects that are not randomly assigned to a treatment. This includes surveys, “natural experiments,” and regression discontinuity designs.
table.blinding: No blinding is involved in this study.
table.research_questions:
Aim 1 (unchanged): AI-assisted systematic reviews will demonstrate methodological and reporting quality comparable to conventional systematic reviews on established appraisal tools, but may exhibit limitations related to transparency and disclosure of AI use.
Aim 2 (revised):We will develop and initially evaluate an evidence-informed, consensus-based, AI-specific critical appraisal instrument for completed systematic reviews. The instrument will assess transparency and assessability alongside AI-related methodological concerns across the systematic review workflow. We anticipate that it will identify concerns not adequately captured by existing general appraisal instruments. Evaluation will focus on content coverage, comprehensibility, inter-rater agreement, and feasibility. As this is an instrument-development study, no formal directional hypothesis is specified for Aim 2.
Aims 3 and 4: Remain unchanged by this amendment.
table.q5: For Aim 2, two trained assessors who were not involved in instrument development will independently evaluate each systematic review in the external evaluation cohort. Assessors will be blinded to one another's ratings, previous Aim 1 judgments, and comparator-tool results. Initial independent judgments will be retained before discussion or adjudication. No experimental treatment assignment or participant blinding is involved.
table.study_design_overview:
This is a multiphase mixed-methods meta-research study comprising four complementary aims.

Aim 1 (unchanged): An observational, between-group comparison of published AI-assisted and conventional systematic reviews. Traditional systematic reviews will be matched to AI-assisted reviews using prespecified characteristics to reduce confounding. Methodological and reporting quality will be compared using established appraisal instruments.

Aim 2 (revised): Development and initial evaluation of an evidence-informed, consensus-based, AI-specific critical appraisal instrument for completed systematic reviews.

The revised Aim 2 will involve four phases:

Evidence integration and candidate development: A focused update of an existing evidence scan, integration of empirical observations from Aim 1 and knowledge-user perspectives from Aim 4, and development of candidate domains and signaling questions.

Modified Delphi consensus: Approximately 20–25 panelists completing two planned anonymous rounds, with a targeted third round if necessary, followed by a focused consensus meeting to refine instrument content, critical flaws, and judgment rules.

Cognitive and developmental testing: Think-aloud testing with approximately 5–8 intended users and developmental appraisal of approximately 15–20 AI-assisted systematic reviews by two independent assessors, with iterative refinement of the instrument and accompanying guidance.

Independent evaluation: Following finalization and locking of the instrument, approximately 30–40 independent AI-assisted systematic reviews will be evaluated by two trained assessors not involved in instrument development. Primary reliability outcomes will include exact agreement on overall judgments and Gwet's AC1 with 95% confidence intervals. Domain-level agreement and feasibility will also be evaluated.

The proposed instrument comprises five provisional domains addressing transparency and assessability, appropriateness and reliability of AI use, evidence identification and selection, data collection and evidence appraisal, and synthesis and interpretation. Appraisal judgments will be categorical and nonadditive.

Aim 3 (unchanged): An experimental mixed design assessing reproducibility of AI-assisted systematic review tasks through repeated runs and comparisons across AI systems and human reviewers.

Aim 4 (unchanged): A qualitative study using semistructured interviews to explore stakeholder perspectives on methodological rigor, transparency, and trust in AI-assisted systematic reviews. Relevant interview findings will additionally inform Aim 2 instrument development without altering the main qualitative study.

Previously specified exploratory analyses using the preliminary AITDI will retain their original definitions. The expanded Aim 2 represents a documented protocol amendment, with completed activities distinguished from prospectively planned procedures.
table.existing_data: Registration prior to analysis of the data
table.existing_data_explanation:
This amendment expands Aim 2 of an ongoing meta-research study. Existing materials include the preliminary AITDI, the published conceptual framework, and empirical observations from Aim 1. Relevant findings from Aim 4 interviews may also inform instrument development.

These materials will contribute to the development of candidate domains and signaling questions. Their prior availability and use will be transparently documented.

The instrument, user manual, judgment rules, and statistical analysis plan will be finalized and locked before the independent evaluation (Cohort 2). Reviews used during development or refinement will be excluded from the independent evaluation sample. Completed activities will be distinguished from procedures planned prospectively under this amendment.
table.data_collection_procedures: Amendment to Aim 2 (October 2026): Development and evaluation of the AI-specific critical appraisal instrument will proceed in four phases. Phase 1 will integrate a focused update of the existing evidence scan with Aim 1 empirical observations, relevant Aim 4 interview contributions, and the preliminary AITDI to develop candidate appraisal questions. Phase 2 will involve a modified Delphi consensus process with multidisciplinary experts and knowledge users, followed by a focused consensus meeting. Phase 3 will involve cognitive testing with intended users and developmental appraisal of a purposively selected sample of AI-assisted systematic reviews. Phase 4 will independently evaluate the finalized instrument in a separate cohort of AI-assisted systematic reviews. Reviews used during development or refinement will be excluded from independent evaluation. The instrument and analysis plan will be locked before this final phase. Full eligibility, sampling, assessment, and evaluation procedures are specified in the revised Aim 2 protocol uploaded to the associated OSF project.
table.sample_size: Revised Aim 2: Approximately 25–30 Delphi panelists will be recruited, aiming for 20–25 completing both planned rounds; approximately 6–10 panelists will participate in the focused consensus meeting. Cognitive testing will involve approximately 5–8 intended users. The developmental appraisal cohort will initially include approximately 15–20 AI-assisted systematic reviews. The independent evaluation cohort will provisionally include approximately 30–40 AI-assisted systematic reviews, each assessed by two trained independent raters who did not participate in instrument development. The final independent evaluation sample size will be determined before sampling using developmental agreement estimates, expected category frequencies, and required precision.
table.measured_variables:
Amendment to Aim 2 (October 2026): Instrument-development measures will include Delphi panel ratings of candidate item importance using a 9-point scale, consensus status according to prespecified thresholds, qualitative feedback on item relevance and comprehensibility, and documentation of modifications to domains, signaling questions, critical flaws, and judgment rules.

Cognitive and developmental testing will assess question interpretation, applicability, missing-information judgments, appraisal time, perceived workload, and reasons for assessor disagreement.

For the independent evaluation, measured variables will include signaling-question responses, applicability decisions, Domain 1 assessability judgments, methodological concern judgments for Domains 2–5, and overall judgments. The provisional overall categories are Low concern, Some concern, High concern, and Insufficient information.

Primary reliability outcomes will be exact agreement on overall judgments and Gwet's AC1 with 95% confidence intervals. Secondary measures will include domain-level agreement, signaling-question responses, applicability disagreements, appraisal time, document-retrieval time, assistance required, unanswerable items, perceived workload, and acceptability.

These measurements relate specifically to the revised Aim 2 and do not replace the previously specified measures for Aims 1, 3, and 4.
table.indices:
The preliminary AITDI will retain its original definitions for previously specified exploratory analyses.

The revised Aim 2 instrument will not generate an additive numerical quality score or index. Instead, it will produce a transparency and assessability judgment, methodological concern judgments across applicable domains, and an overall categorical judgment.

Numerical codes may be used for data management and agreement analyses but will not represent appraisal points or weights. Delphi importance ratings will inform instrument development rather than contribute to a numerical appraisal score.
table.statistical_tests:
Amendment to Aim 2 (October 2026): The revised Aim 2 will develop and initially evaluate an AI-specific critical appraisal instrument using consensus methods, cognitive testing, developmental appraisal, and independent evaluation.

During the modified Delphi process, candidate items will be rated for importance on a 9-point scale. Consensus for inclusion will require at least 70% of valid ratings in the 7–9 range and no more than 15% in the 1–3 range. Consensus for exclusion will require at least 70% in the 1–3 range and no more than 15% in the 7–9 range. Other distributions will indicate no consensus. Rating distributions, denominators, missing responses, and disagreements will be reported.

Cognitive and developmental testing will examine comprehensibility, applicability, usability, and sources of assessor disagreement. Agreement estimates obtained with different developmental versions will be reported separately.

For the independent evaluation, primary reliability outcomes will be exact agreement on the overall appraisal judgment and Gwet's AC1 with 95% confidence intervals. Domain-level agreement will be a key secondary outcome. Paired judgment tables and category frequencies will describe disagreement patterns.

The primary reliability analysis will treat overall judgments as nominal because Insufficient information is not ordinal relative to Low, Some, and High concern. Supplementary weighted AC2 or weighted kappa analyses may be undertaken when both assessors provide Low, Some, or High concern judgments. Reliability analyses will use initial independent ratings and account for repeated assessments by the same raters where relevant.

Feasibility outcomes will include appraisal time, document-retrieval time, assistance required, unanswerable items, perceived workload, and acceptability. Exploratory comparisons with ROBIS and, where applicable, AMSTAR 2 may examine overlap and potential added value, without treating either as a reference standard.

The instrument, guidance, judgment rules, and analysis plan will be finalized and locked before the independent evaluation. Previously specified analyses of the preliminary AITDI will retain their original definitions.

Supplementary weighted AC2 or weighted kappa analyses may be undertaken when both assessors provide Low, Some, or High concern judgments. Reliability analyses will use initial independent ratings and account for repeated assessments by the same raters where relevant.

Feasibility outcomes will include appraisal time, document-retrieval time, assistance required, unanswerable items, perceived workload, and acceptability. Exploratory comparisons with ROBIS and, where applicable, AMSTAR 2 may examine overlap and potential added value, without treating either as a reference standard.

The instrument, guidance, judgment rules, and analysis plan will be finalized and locked before the independent evaluation.
